brief:
The executive director of the Jewish Federations of North America, Eric Fingerhut, described results from U.S. midterm elections as "complicated," Shehab Wire reported. Fingerhut's characterization reflects growing anxiety within both major American political parties regarding Israel policy.

The assessment signals deepening divisions over Middle East issues among Democratic and Republican voters, with Jewish organizations monitoring shifting attitudes toward Israeli positions across the political spectrum.

title: American Jewish groups report rising concern over Israel among both U.S. parties
